subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Egyptian Duat
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Egyptian Duat usable.

hook.text: Egyptian dead traveled the Duat—a perilous underworld of gates, monsters, and spells lasting twelve hours.

buildup.text: The Book of the Dead was a literal travel guide. Spells, maps, and passwords for navigating the afterlife.

discovery.text: Each gate had a guardian demanding a password. Without the right words, the soul was stuck forever.

twist.text: The wealthy bought better Books of the Dead. Even in Egypt's afterlife, money bought a smoother journey.

climax.text: The Duat was the most detailed afterlife map ever drawn. Egyptians treated death like a foreign country.

punchline.text: Pack your spells. The journey is long.

quiz.question: What was the Egyptian Book of the Dead?
options: A guide for navigating the afterlife
